# Native TileLang FlexAttention

This experimental implementation lowers PyTorch FlexAttention to a native
Inductor template on Huawei Ascend 950. TileLang is an optional dependency;
the default implementation remains Triton.

## Run the example

Use a matching PyTorch / torch_npu 2.14 installation containing this change,
Triton-Ascend for surrounding pointwise kernels, and the Huawei Ascend TileLang
backend with `SimtVF`, `SimdVF`, `dual_copy`, and automatic pipelining support.
Load the matching CANN runtime and compiler environment first. A standard GPU
TileLang or Triton installation is not a substitute for these backends.

The implementation was validated with TileLang revision `79eaaae3` plus local
SDK integration changes. That revision alone is not a reproducible installation
specification; a compatible backend build and CANN toolchain are required.

Select an allocated physical device, then run:

```bash
export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<allocated-device>
export ASCEND_VISIBLE_DEVICES="$ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES"
export TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1
python -P examples/flex_attention/dense.py
```

The example selects `config.flex_attention.implementation = "tilelang"`, compiles
with `backend="inductor"`, and compares the full output with an independent FP32
reference. The first call includes compilation. Select `"triton"` to use the
existing implementation.

## Supported contract

- Inference with the Python wrapper; one attention output.
- Contiguous, static BF16 Q/K/V on the same NPU, with matching batch/head counts.
- Q `[B, H, M, 128]`, K/V `[B, H, N, 128]`; positive M/N divisible by 128.
- Each Q/K/V tensor must contain fewer than `2**31` elements.
- Finite static scale, supported scalar score/mask callbacks, and BlockMask
  partial/full block lists. Callback support is explicitly checked in
  `torch_npu/_inductor/kernel/tilelang_fx.py`.

Backward, GQA/MQA, captured tensors, symbolic shapes, auxiliary outputs,
noncontiguous inputs, other head dimensions/dtypes, template fusion,
multi-candidate autotuning, C++ wrappers, and AOTInductor are not supported.
Unsupported inputs fail explicitly instead of silently selecting another backend.

Lowering builds a `TileLangTemplateBuffer`. Scheduling renders specialized
TileLang source and registers compilation in the wrapper initialization phase;
execution launches the prepared kernel. Softmax uses SIMD. The default dense
specialization removes SIMT callbacks and enables pipelining; generic callbacks
retain serial sparse traversal.

## Regression tests and diagnostics

With the matching installed torch_npu wheel, run the device-free regression suite:

```bash
python -P test/_inductor/test_tilelang_flex_attention_native.py
```

These tests exercise lowering, scheduling, source specialization, cache identity,
rejection behavior, and launch lifecycle using a mocked device launch. They do
not establish NPU numerical correctness; the example requires a real device.

`TORCH_COMPILE_DEBUG=1` enables Inductor traces. Setting
`FLEX_TILELANG_ARTIFACT_DIR` to a writable diagnostic directory additionally saves
rendered source, device code, and compilation/launch records. Diagnostics are
disabled by default. Kernel attribution is retained in
`torch_npu/_inductor/kernel/LICENSE.tilelang`.
